question: Out of every 1,000 people on Earth, how many are homeless or living without adequate shelter?
answer_explanation: Roughly 14 out of every 1,000 people worldwide lack adequate shelter. That represents around 112 million people — a figure that spans street homelessness, displacement camps, and severe informal housing across every continent. The true scale is likely higher, as many countries lack consistent counting methods.

relationship_fact.text: Africa accounts for the largest share of global homelessness — more than 6 out of every 1,000 global citizens experience homelessness or severe housing precarity there, compared to less than 1 per 1,000 in Europe or North America.

temporal_fact.text: Global homelessness has worsened since 2000. Estimates suggested around 100 million people lacked adequate shelter then; today that figure exceeds 150 million, driven by rapid urbanisation, conflict displacement, and climate-related housing loss.

anchor_fact.text: There are approximately 8 billion people on Earth. Even a tiny fraction — say, 0.01% — represents 800,000 people. The homeless population is estimated at well over 100 million, which is roughly 1.4% of the world population.
